text:
morgan: Quick question — noticed some clients crashing when calling /v1/predict. In a few cases the server returns a JSON that either has "result": null or just omits "result" entirely. SDK's deserializer trips on the omission. anyone seen this recently?

ciara: yeah saw one error from logs a couple hours ago. can you paste the exact responses?

morgan: here are two examples from staging: 
```
// case A (null)
{
  "id": "req-123",
  "model": "redwood-2",
  "result": null
}

// case B (omitted)
{
  "id": "req-124",
  "model": "redwood-2"
}
```

ashley: hm, SDK expects the key to exist and maps it to Option<T> but our JSON parser path treats missing key as error in one of the generated structs. That was on the 1.2.0 SDK generator.

jorge: also note we received a few responses with Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8 which made some clients bail before JSON parsing. suspect middleware fallback in the canary runtime.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T14:42:01 by @infra-team to staging.

sam: TL;DR: two issues — header mismatch (content-type) and inconsistent presence of the field. For contract safety we should pick one canonical behaviour and enforce it server-side. My vote: always include the key and use null for empty/failed generation. that's explicit and easier for typed clients.

ciara: +1 to always present the key. also we should document that clients must accept null or an array, but server providing the key is better.

ashley: agreed. Implementation notes:
- API layer: normalize response to include "result": null when we have no output.
- middleware: ensure Content-Type header is set to application/json for all 2xx responses.
- add a contract test in our e2e suite that rejects text/plain.

morgan: sounds good. can we add a json-schema validation step in the response path? simple check against schema that requires "result" to be present (nullable).

jorge: easy to add a lightweight jsonschema check in the response pipeline. cost is tiny, and it will catch stray middleware changes. i'll draft a PR to runtime that validates and adds the header.

ashley: on the SDK side i'll update the generator to tolerate missing keys (map to Option) but keep behavior consistent once server enforces the presence. that way older SDKs won't crash immediately.

sam: compatibility plan:
- server: change to always include key and header. roll out as non-breaking (present key = null is safe).
- SDK: release patch that tolerates omission for older clients.
- tests: add contract test (json-schema) and a few integration tests asserting Content-Type.
- rollout: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring on parse-fail metric.

ciara: do we need an API changelog entry? even though behavior is backwards-compatible, worth posting a note under /docs/api/compat.

morgan: yes, i'll open a tiny docs PR referencing the schema and example responses. include example curl like:
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/predict | jq '.'
// will always include "result": null | [ ... ]
```

deploy-bot: canary created: app/runtime v2.14.1 canary @ 5%

ashley: i'll pick up the SDK change, target patch 1.2.1. sending draft PR now.

jorge: PR for runtime schema-check coming in ~1hr, will add tests.

ciara: i'll add monitoring alert: metric parse_failures > 0.5% over 5m during rollout -> rollback.

morgan: perfect. assigning reviewers: @sam @ciara @ashley. thanks all :thumbsup:
